sections.text: Introduction

We recommend a periodic inspection of the tap changer
 equipment to certain a high reliability in service according to manufacture
 instructions.
 Also, we recommend that personnel well acquainted with the equipment should
 carry out the inspection.
 The Inspection should be carried out as quickly as possible with the most care
 and tidiness.

The first draft was initiated by eng. Emad Mabrouk 
Mohamed, 
and tested by eng. Wagdy Mechaiel Barsoum at El-Minia132kv substation, accepted 
by eng Metawie Aly Hassan General director, and approved by eng. Ahmed Saied 
MPIS and QC General Director at ME zone

The maintenance of 
 the OLTC consist of 3 stages:
1) Inspection:

On the rating plate, 
 inspection once a year, is recommended. This principally concerns the 
 motor-drive mechanism and refers to a visual inspection inside the motor 
 cabinet to check that nothing is loose, the heater is functioning the 
 contactor contacts are not burned in the motor-drive mechanism a counter 
 registers every tap-changer operation. During inspection the counter is read. 
 If possible, motor and counter are tested by operating one step and than back. 
 If the OLTC has its own oil conservator, the breather and the oil level 
 indicator are checked. The inspection is carried out while the transformer is 
 in service
2) Overhaul

The contact life and 
 the frequency of operations determine the time interval between overhauls. The 
 number of operation run by the OLTC is recorded by a counter, housed in the 
 motor. Mechanism cabinet the registered number of operations should be noted 
 at every inspection and overhaul. The OLTC should normally be overhauled 
 regularly at intervals of 1/5 of the estimated contact life. Therevelant 
 information is stated on the rating-plate. Hereby, the contact wear can be 
 followed and necessary preparations can be made for replacing the contacts.
3) Contact Replacement

On the rating plate 
 of the OLTC the calculated contact life at rated load is stated the contacts 
 will withstand a very larg number of switching operations for normal power 
 transformers the number of operations of the diverter switch is approximately 
 20 per day, which means that exchange of the contacts is not normaly necessary 
 during the life of the transformer

Caution: The number 
 of operations must be in no case exceed 500,000 due to weakening spring 
 tension of the contacts.
Safety Precautions
A work permit must be issued,

Safety rope with caution marks surrounding 
 the work area is required.

items: A work permit must be issued,
Personnel carrying out the maintenance should carry the suitable safety category, should be trained and qualified or directly supervised by someone who is.

Safety rope with caution marks surrounding 
 the work area is required.

Wear your safety helmet, gloves, glasses and 
 shoes,

The high voltage CB, low voltage CB of the transformer must be isolated
 & proper earthing at the two sides is required
Use only fiberglass ladders

Be sure to ground the transformer bushing terminals with on-site grounding
 equipment and with ancillary grounding cable of a thickness specified by
 on-site regulations.
Caution marks in control room is required.

sections.text: Work to be Carried Out

rows:
Operate the tap changer electrically in both directions
 from the operation box of the transformer and from control room to prove
 motor operation

Place local remote switch to the local position to prevent
 any unauthorized operations.

Determine the neutral position or adjustment position (centre
 position of the tap changer)
Operate the tap changer to the adjustment position
Cut off AC current of the tap changer operation motor

Confirm operating position in inspection glass on the tap
 changer cover
Close valve between the tap changer and conservator tank

Connect the flange of filtering machine drain hose to the
 flange of tap changer drain valve
Open the tap changer bleeder valve in the head cover.

Start operating the pump of the filtering machine when the
 bleeder has been opened and. removes on third of the oil from the tap
 changer compartment.

Remove the guard plate of the horizontal transmission
 shaft by releasing the two clamps that fix the beginning and the end of
 the cover and slide them to the bevel gear end of the shaft

Remove the transmission shaft by releasing the coupling
 clamp that connects it with the tap changers. 
 Figure 1.

Clean the surface cover for the tap changer and the area
 of the main cover for the transformer that surrounding the tap changer
 cover.

Unscrew the 24 screws of the tap changer cover after
 ensuring the oil is lowered enough and collect all screws. Washers, nuts
 and lock washers in a tin can.

Drain 2/3 of the oil quantity and leave the rest in the
 diverter switch oil compartment for the first cleaning, and shut down the
 filtering machine.

Erect the davit or mobile crane into position. Before
 proceeding with erection of the davit or moving the mobile crane, ensure
 the crane operator is fully aware of neighboring live apparatus and the
 safe limits of approach to overhead lines or bus bars, and the crane is
 grounded.

Lift the cover of the tap changer complete with qualitrol
 safety and set it securely to one side, be careful not to allow something
 fallen into the oil compartment device and check the aluminum explosion
 vent for signs of corrosion or damage.

Check red marks on the gear plate, gear and tap changer
 head

Line up tap changer head and cog wheel, plate and Geneva
 wheel and dial marks to ensure proper alignment.

Undo suction pipe connection being careful not to drop the
 washer. Move the suction pipe to the right or left direction, to loosen
 it, then pull the nipple out of the pipe.

Release the two energy springs by raising the two locking
 pins by using an 8mm screw. screw the screw into the head of the locking
 pin and pull the blocking pin from it's slot to release the spring. 
 Figure 12, 13, 14.

Release the upper gear unit by releasing 5 screws, every
 screw has one washer and one lock washer Be careful not to allow them to
 fall into the oil compartment and check gear marks on the upper gear unit
 to detect it's position before raising it.(use socket wrench 13)

Take not of the 2 guide pins in the tap changer head and
 the two triangle marks on top of the tap changer insert for
 reinstallation.

Remove suction pipe using screwdriver or key to pry off
 pipe from the bottom bearing. Fig. 15

Very carefully raise up the suction pipe vertically,
 taking care not to break it.

Attach operating key to the insert coupling face in order
 to centralize the moveable changeover selector contact and facilitate
 removal of the insert. Figure 16, 17

Using the davit or crane attach the chain hoist and 1/2
 inch shackles to the lugs on the diverted switch. 
 Figure 18

Carefully and very slowly lift the diverter switch clear
 of the oil compartment by turning it clockwise and counterclockwise to
 miss the contacts on the housing and the switching unit from hitting one
 another and wait for several minutes to allow the oil to drip.

Pull a plastic garbage bag over the diverter to prevent
 drips while lowering to ground level.

Drain oil compartment and clean with a 400-mm brush, flush
 with new transformer oil and drain.

Examine oil compartment with mirror and check for
 electrical damage such as tracking, partial discharge and mechanical
 failures.

Replace the tap changer head cover to prevent ingress of
 moisture, dust or something else

Work must be done in a clean area with the ground covered
 with a clean sheet of plastic and a proper steel or plastic tray over the
 plastic sheet is required to clean the diverted switch and selector with
 oil in it.
Clean suction pipe with 40 mm brush

Check spring movement of roller contacts on switching
 element.

Check wear of roller contacts and measure with a vernier
 calibrator. Compare measurements to chart for type Y tap-changers. Replace
 all contacts if one contact does not meet the minimum requirement or if
 contacts will wear below the minimum requirement before next overhaul.

Measure transition resistor from the middle roller to
 either side. Deviatioshould not exceed 10% of the resistor value. 
 Figure 36
Remove carbon from the contacts with a scubbing pad.

Reinstall the OL TC insert in the reverse order of its
 removal using the operating key to lift the insert.

If the tap changer has a change over selector switch move
 the OL TC to a position where the moveable change over selector contacts
 will be situated between phases after the installation.

If the tap changer does not have a change over selector
 switch move the OL TC insert so that it will be approximately in the
 adjustment position after its installation.

Lower the OL TC insert into the oil compartment making
 sure the clearance between the grading rings as well as parts of the
 switching elements and the fixed parts of the oil compartment is
 sufficient.

Remove the operating key and insert suction pipe. OLTC
 insert will be centered in the oil compartment by pressing the top end of
 the suction pipe.

Reinstall the gear unit setting it at the adjustment
 position in accordance with the position indicating disk and the gear
 markings. Attach gear unit with bolts.

Install the tap changer cover and replace gasket if
 necessary.

Check the adjustment position through the inspection
 window in the cover.
Refill the tap changer with oil

Reconnect the drive shaft and guard cover torching
 coupling bolts to 9nm. Check entire drive shaft for wear and binding.
 Clearance between couplings must be approximately 2-3 mm.

Operate the tap changer by hand to ensure correct
 installment.

Check the number of turns between tap changes by cranking
 the tap changer from a raise to a lower and back to a raise position. The
 turns must not be greater than one. If the turns are greater than one use
 the following steps:
 a) Turn the crank handle clockwise from
 position 10 to position 9 until the diverter switch operates and count
 the crank handle revolutions necessary for the red mark to appear in
 the green section in the middle of the inspection.
 b) Turn the crank handle counterclockwise
 from position 9 to position 10 until the diverter switch operates and
 count the crank handle revolutions necessary for the red mark to
 appear in green section in the middle of the inspection glass.
 c)
 Note the difference between the counted
 crank handle revolutions
 d) To correct any revolutions greater than
 one by divided by 2 and turning the crank in the direction of the most
 turns after uncoupling the drive shaft.
 e) Re-couple the motor drive at vertical part
 of the driving shaft Figure 1.
 f) Repeat steps I and 2 to verify the same
 number of turns in each direction

Operate the OL TC mechanically through the complete
 operating cycle to check its function

When satisfied with the mechanical operation check tap
 changer electrically.
Restore tap changer to tap position before maintenance
Place tap changer selector on remote operation.

sections.text: The Disc Brake

Wipe the 
brake disc free from grease.

Check that 
the cam disc on the "one-turn" shaft iose not affect the driving roller in the 
maintaining contact after an operation. The moving energy in the motor and the 
toothed wheels should be absorbed by the brake, and the motor-drive mechanism 
should stop with the red mark 25º from the centre of the brake pads. This can 
be adjusted by tightening both of the spring bolts on the brake.

Using the 
hand-crank, operate the motor-drive mechanism until the bake is fully open. At 
this point the length of the springs must not be less than 35 mm. If the brake 
still dose not function, oil or grease has entered the brake linings, which will 
then need cleaning.

sections.text: Clean as follows:

Using a 
pair of tongs, remove the roll pins that hold the supporting shafts on the brake 
blocks.

Then remove 
the shaft and the brake blocks.

Clean the 
brake linings on the two brake with degreasing agent.

When 
refitting the brake. Check that the brake disc is completely free from grease.

Adjust the 
spring force of the brake until the motor-drive mechanism stops within the 
tolerances given above.

Check that 
the brake for the maintaining contact prevents the arm system on the maintaining 
contact shaft from swinging beyond its normal position when the roller on the 
driving arm moves free from the cam disc. At the end of the operation, contacts 
for operation in the opposite driection shall not move when the arm system 
swings back to wards its normal position.

Un permitted swinging should be prevented by 
raising the braking force, i.e. tightening the spring bolt. An increasing spring 
force on the brake makes the maintaining contact arm swing back faster, and the 
brake for the maintaining contact must be adjusted.

sections.text: Lubrication

The bearing points of the brake blocks and the 
links should be sparingly lubricated with oil. (Use oil for plain ball and 
roller bearings.) The spur gears, the genevs wheel with the limit stop, the cam 
discs and the cam bar are sparingly lubricated with grease when necessary. (Us 
lithiurn grease for ball and roller bearings in low temperature (-50-+ 
80ºC)(-58-+176ºF) Other bearing points do not need lubrication

Note: Protect the brake disc and the brake linings 
against lubricarts. Wipe off excess lubricant
Operation test

Operate the 
driving mechanism first by manual operation and then electrically between the 
limit positions.

Check the 
limit stops by operating the OLTC to one of the end positions. When trying to 
operate it electrically beyond the end position, the motor should not start.

Check the 
mechanical end stop by trying to hand crank it beyond the end position. After a 
couple of turns on the hand crank it should be mechanically stopped.

Operate the 
OLTC electrically to the other end position and carry out the same test 
procedure as above

 position 10 to position 9 until the diverter switch operates and count
 the crank handle revolutions necessary for the red mark to appear in
 the green section in the middle of the inspection.
 b) Turn the crank handle counterclockwise
 from position 9 to position 10 until the diverter switch operates and
 count the crank handle revolutions necessary for the red mark to
 appear in green section in the middle of the inspection glass.
 c)
 Note the difference between the counted
 crank handle revolutions
 d) To correct any revolutions greater than
 one by divided by 2 and turning the crank in the direction of the most
 turns after uncoupling the drive shaft.
 e) Re-couple the motor drive at vertical part
 of the driving shaft Figure 1.
 f) Repeat steps I and 2 to verify the same
 number of turns in each direction
